input.value: Basement flooded with approximately 2 inches of water across entire floor
Hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked up to 1 foot high, stored boxes ruined

input.question: What caused the basement flooding—was it from your home's plumbing (burst pipe, failed sump pump, etc.) or from external water intrusion (heavy rain, groundwater, neighbor's issue)?

input.rationale: Claimant's own plumbing failed, causing direct damage to the home's interior structure (hardwood floor, drywall) and contents (stored boxes).

Basement-wide water damage affecting multiple building components (flooring, drywall, contents) typically exceeds $25,000; hardwood and drywall restoration plus content replacement is substantial and requires on-site adjuster assessment.

input.claim_summary: Homeowner Sam Patel (POL-1004) returned from work trip to find basement flooded with 2 inches of water caused by plumbing failure. Damage includes buckled hardwood floor, drywall soaked up to 1 foot, and ruined stored contents. High-severity claim requiring on-site adjuster assessment and water damage mitigation coordination.
